guide: Add a commit-time check to Claude Code so broken code is caught before a pull request reaches GitHub. You need Claude Code, a GitHub repository and a test or lint command your project already runs.
1. Decide what "not broken" means for your project, for example the tests pass, the linter is clean and the build succeeds.
1. Put those checks behind one command you can run locally, such as an npm script or a Makefile target.
1. Package the checks as a Claude Code plugin, bundling the rules Claude should follow and the tools it may call, such as a skill or a command that runs your checks.
1. Add a hook in the plugin that fires when Claude is about to commit, runs the check command and blocks the commit if it fails.
1. Install the plugin for everyone on the team, for example through a shared plugin marketplace or by committing the plugin settings to the repository.
1. Commit a deliberately broken change on a test branch and confirm the commit is stopped and Claude is told why.
1. Once it behaves, let Claude fix the failure and commit again so the pull request goes to GitHub only after the checks pass.
Watch out: a plugin only guards sessions where it is installed, so keep a matching check in GitHub Actions as a backstop for anyone who commits without it.

```
You are helping me set up a Claude Code plugin that stops broken code reaching GitHub. My project uses <language and framework>, my repository is hosted on GitHub, and my team works in Claude Code. The command that proves the code is healthy is <test, lint and build command>.
Build a plugin that contains: a short set of rules telling Claude to run that command before every commit and to fix failures instead of skipping them; a hook that runs the command when Claude attempts a commit and blocks the commit if it fails, returning the error output to Claude; and a manifest so the plugin can be installed from a shared marketplace or from the repository.
Constraints: no secrets in the plugin files, use only the documented Claude Code plugin and hook formats, and keep the checks fast enough to run on every commit. If <my checks take longer than a minute>, suggest which to run on commit and which to leave to CI.
Return the full file tree, the contents of every file, the exact install steps for a teammate, and a short test I can run to prove a failing change is blocked.
```
